title: Ghost A/B mapping left in edge cache caused rollback stall and capacity oscillation
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: During a canary rollout of model v2.3 on 2026-02-28, a partial routing config apply left stale A/B target mappings cached in edge routers. A small fraction of traffic continued to hit the old mapping (ghost traffic), which produced noisy health signals that triggered an automated rollback. The rollback could not complete because a long-lived version pin remained set by a prior manual operation. Manual cache invalidation and an emergency unpin were required to finish the rollback. The incident lasted ~37 minutes and caused elevated tail latency and capacity oscillation on Dedicated pools in eu region.
timeline: 2026-02-28T15:12Z - Canary rollout started for model v2.3 (10% weight).
2026-02-28T15:17Z - Alerts: 95th/99th latency increase on region-eu-dedicated observed (INC-4107).
2026-02-28T15:22Z - Canary healthchecks failed; automated promotion aborted and rollback initiated.
2026-02-28T15:24Z - Investigation: traffic split metrics show persistent ~0.3% of traffic hitting obsolete A/B mapping not present in latest control-plane config.
2026-02-28T15:28Z - Rollback controller reported pin_lock_conflict; rollback stalled because version pin remained set with unknown owner.
2026-02-28T15:45Z - Engineers performed targeted cache invalidation on edge routers and executed emergency unpin; rollback completed at 15:49Z.
2026-02-28T15:50Z - Latency returned to baseline by 15:55Z; incident declared resolved at 16:10Z and postmortem channel opened.
2026-03-01 - This follow-up ticket created to track fixes and mitigations.
impact_summary: Duration: ~37 minutes of elevated latency and increased cost for impacted requests.
Surface: Dedicated eu capacity and rollout telemetry for the canary.
Customer impact: Higher tail latency for some customers; a small number of support tickets received. No model output correctness or data exposure issues found.
Operational impact: Manual reconciliation required, SRE and Edge team intervention for cache invalidation and unpin.
evidence: Edge router traces: trace-20260228-15-4621..4668 (edge logs archived under logs/edge/2026-02-28).
Controller logs: rollout-controller error entries with 'pin_lock_conflict' (logs/runtime/controller/2026-02-28/canary.log).
Dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood/platform/incidents/INC-4107 showing latency spike and traffic split chart.
Support ticket: SUP-7249 filed during the incident reporting high latency.
root_causes: Control-plane applied routing changes via a non-atomic path that allowed edge routers to briefly retain previous A/B mappings (partial apply race).
Version pins could be set manually and had no default TTL; rollback controller does not force-unpin after a timeout.
Lack of a direct metric to identify stale-route residue slowed diagnosis and delayed automated remediation.
postmortem_conclusions: A race between control-plane config apply and edge router cache reconciliation produced ghost traffic to obsolete mappings.
Rollback automation assumed pins are short-lived; durable manual pins combined with stale-route residue can deadlock rollbacks.
Preflight checks and stronger observability around stale mappings would prevent similar incidents.

mitigation_plan: Short term (0-2w): Deploy emergency unpin script to ops toolkit, add temporary dashboard panels for stale_route_rate, and require manual preflight in next canary launches.
Medium term (1-2m): Implement two-phase atomic swap for routing updates in control-plane, pin TTLs, and forced-unpin escalation path in controller.
Long term (quarter): Build synthetic preflight harness that probes edge caches across regions before enabling canary weights >0 and integrate into CI for release validation.
review_feedback: Design review (2026-03-04): SRE asked pin TTL be configurable by project; runtime team recommends cluster-default with optional override flag.
Security review: No secrets involved; request to add audit events for manual unpin operations and include them in org-wide audit logs.
PM feedback: Prepare a short customer-facing incident note for affected customers summarizing impact, root cause, and mitigations; coordinate with Support for targeted outreach.
